findings.claim: configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh verification step confirms only that a ruleset with the correct name exists; it does not assert that the ruleset's `conditions.ref_name.include` contains `refs/tags/renovate/v*` nor that the `rules` array includes all three required rule types (deletion, non_fast_forward, update). A stale environment where a previous invocation created a same-named ruleset with different env-var overrides (e.g., `SCP_RENOVATE_TAG_PATTERN=renovate/v1` instead of `renovate/v*`) would pass verification while leaving the tag namespace partially uncovered.
findings.evidence: scripts/configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh lines 88-95: `final_id=$(… jq -r --arg name "$RULESET_NAME" '.[] | select(.name == $name) | .id' …)` — selects only by `.name`; ruleset body fields `conditions` and `rules` are never read back. Compare with configure-020j-protections.sh lines 143-152: same presence-only check; 020J has the same limitation but was previously accepted for a stable, already-exercised ruleset. 020F is a NEW script introduced by fix-round-1 and has not been exercised against a live repo yet, so the gap is newly introduced here.
findings.impact: Low probability in practice (single-operator estate, env vars default to correct values). If triggered, the `renovate/v*` tags would be under-protected without any runtime signal — the script exits 0 while attestation `CRIT-SAFE-001 closed` is false. An auditor relying on the script's exit code as evidence of closure would be misled.
findings.mitigation: After the `final_id` non-empty check, add a jq assertion that reads the full ruleset and verifies `conditions.ref_name.include` contains an element matching the expected pattern prefix: `gh api repos/${REPO}/rulesets/${final_id} | jq -e --arg pat "refs/tags/${TAG_PATTERN}" '.conditions.ref_name.include | map(select(. == $pat)) | length > 0'`. This aligns the verification depth with what the verification comment claims.

findings.claim: DISPATCH-NOTE.md §(vii) verification block cites existing Dependabot PRs (#42, #43, #44) as corroborating evidence for Mend Renovate app installation. Dependabot (GitHub-native, triggered by `.github/dependabot.yml`) and Mend Renovate (third-party GitHub App, independent installation) are entirely separate tools; the existence of Dependabot-opened PRs provides zero logical evidence that the Mend Renovate GitHub App is installed on the `jrnb2024` account or the target repo.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md lines 61-65: `Mend Renovate app installation is verified by the existence of .github/dependabot.yml PRs already on the repo (#42, #43, #44 Dependabot bumps observed pre-Threshold-A)`. The PRs named are explicitly labelled as Dependabot bumps; the verification conflates two independent bots. The Mend dashboard URL cited (`developer.mend.io/github/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane`) is the only Renovate-specific evidence.
findings.impact: Not a runtime correctness defect; however a future auditor reading the DISPATCH-NOTE closure evidence for `U-gov-1 / Renovate-installed` could be confused or could incorrectly apply the same reasoning to a repo where Renovate is NOT installed but Dependabot is. Evidence quality is load-bearing for governance closure.
findings.mitigation: Remove or parenthesise the Dependabot PR citation in the Renovate installation evidence block. The primary evidence (Mend dashboard URL) is sufficient on its own. If belt-and-suspenders evidence is desired, the correct corroborating artefact is a `gh api /app/installations` response showing the Mend Renovate App ID, or the Renovate Dependency Dashboard issue auto-created by Renovate in the repo upon first run.

Regex `v?[0-9][^\s]*` matches: `v` (optional v), `1` (first digit), `.0.0` (non-whitespace run). `currentDigest` group matches the 40-char SHA exactly. Multi-line bridge `[\s\S]*?` is lazy and reaches first `uses:` across the line boundary. Match confirmed.

r1_additional_verifications.check: (2) renovate/default.json JSON validity and schema semantics
r1_additional_verifications.detail: JSON is syntactically well-formed. `$schema` URL `https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json` is the canonical Renovate schema endpoint. Root `ignoreUnstable: true` plus packageRule `ignoreUnstable: false` is a valid per-rule override per Renovate docs. Dual `automerge: false` (root + packageRule) is redundant-but-consistent, not contradictory.
Renovate interprets `prHourlyLimit: 0` as no throttle (unlimited). The field is valid inside the `vulnerabilityAlerts` context; Renovate supports per-context overrides of global rate limits.
For a tag `v1.0.0`, Renovate's `{{newValue}}` expands to `v1.0.0` (the v is part of the tag name). URL becomes `…/releases/tag/v1.0.0`. No double-v. COR-004 confirmed closed.

Bash syntax valid; `set -euo pipefail` present; `require_cmd` guards on `gh` and `jq`; heredoc uses unquoted `<<JSON` for intentional variable expansion (same pattern as 020J); `TAG_PATTERN` glob-wildcard `renovate/v*` is not subject to pathname expansion inside heredoc body (bash guarantee). Idempotency: name-presence check before POST. Structure mirrors 020J. One correctness gap raised as COR-R2-001.

`exclude-patterns` is nested correctly under the group name `gh-actions-minor-patch` at the same level as `patterns` and `update-types`. GitHub Dependabot docs confirm wildcard support in `exclude-patterns`. `actions/setup-*` is a valid glob matching `actions/setup-node`, `actions/setup-python`, etc. Action names are spelled correctly.

TF-020F-001 through TF-020F-004 appear in both DISPATCH-NOTE.md (tracked-forward section) and FIX-ROUND-1.md (tracked-forward items section). Descriptions are consistent. No orphan IDs in either document.
Item (iii) is correctly unticked with explicit `POST-MERGE step` annotation. All other items correctly reflect delivered artefacts. Checklist state is consistent with the actual file set in this PR.
